title: Planar isotopy of link diagrams
statement: Two regular oriented link diagrams $D,D'$ are **planar isotopic** when there is an orientation-preserving ambient isotopy of the plane carrying the decorated immersed graph of $D$ to that of $D'$, preserving over/under data and strand orientations; a **planar isotopy of diagrams** is a jointly smooth one-parameter family all of whose members are diagrams, each obtained from the previous one by such an ambient isotopy. In Reidemeister's theorem planar isotopies are admitted as moves; no crossing is created or destroyed along them.
strategy: Planar isotopies are the moves that carry a regular projection between exceptional times of a general-position isotopy; they are separated from the three local moves R1-R3 in the theorem statement.

references.title: Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, AMS Surveys and Monographs 208 (2015); section 2.1 and Appendix B.1, printed pp. 367-372
Queffelec, Reidemeister's theorem using transversality, Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society (2024); arXiv:2406.18203v1, sections 2-3
